headline: The Bot That Makes Money No Matter Which Way Bitcoin Moves
lede: On Polymarket, the world's largest prediction-market exchange, an anonymous automated trader known as gabagool22 accumulated close to $800,000 in roughly three months by exploiting a structural loophole in short-duration Bitcoin contracts — buying both sides of a binary bet simultaneously, below the guaranteed settlement payout, and collecting the difference. A writeup promoted by the X account @thejayden brought the strategy to wide public attention. It now faces extinction by fee.
body:
**Polymarket** is a blockchain-based prediction market where users trade on the outcomes of real-world events — elections, sports results, commodity prices — with each share priced between one cent and 99 cents to reflect implied probability. The platform runs on the Polygon network and settles trades in *USDC*, a dollar-pegged stablecoin, operating a peer-to-peer *central limit order book* rather than acting as a counterparty itself. In 2024 it processed roughly $9 billion in total volume; by 2025 that figure topped $10 billion, with sports markets accounting for the majority of open interest.

Within that landscape, a pseudonymous operator known as gabagool22 attracted unusual attention. The account racked up cumulative profits approaching $800,000 across roughly three months, executing an estimated 100,000 trades per day — nearly all automated. The method was *intramarket spread capture* in Polymarket's Bitcoin 15-minute *binary* markets: short-duration contracts that pay either $1 (yes) or $0 (no) based on whether BTC closes above a given price at a specified moment.

The core insight is a mathematical identity. Because one of YES or NO must always settle at $1.00, any pair purchased for less than a dollar combined locks in guaranteed profit regardless of which way Bitcoin moves. In practice, thin liquidity and emotional retail trading momentarily push one side of the order book below fair value, creating pairs acquirable for 96 or 97 cents. A bot monitoring the book in real time, buying both legs when their sum dips below parity, and holding through settlement 15 minutes later, pockets the gap as riskless return. One documented transaction showed a combined pair cost of $0.966 — a 3.4% return in under a quarter-hour. At 100,000 daily executions across dozens of simultaneous markets, those margins aggregate into substantial sums.

Polymarket's response was structural. In January 2026 the platform introduced a dynamic *taker fee* that peaks at roughly 3.15% for crypto contracts trading near 50 cents — precisely the zone where spread-capture bots hunt for mispricings. A fee of that magnitude consumes nearly the entire profit margin the strategy depends on. Fourteen of the twenty most profitable accounts on Polymarket's public leaderboard are estimated to be bots; the fee redesign was explicitly intended to redirect some of that extracted value back to the *market makers* who supply liquidity.

Whether gabagool22 adapted after the fee change is unknown — the account is anonymous, carries no confirmed social presence, and its strategy can only be inferred from public on-chain settlement data. What is clear is that @thejayden's article publicizing the approach arrived at a peculiar moment: shortly before the platform introduced charges designed with exactly this strategy in mind. The subsequent wave of copycat implementations — the poster claims 50-plus DMs from people who built working bots — now operates against a fee structure engineered to make such copying unprofitable.

concepts.definition: An exchange where participants buy and sell contracts tied to the outcome of future events. Prices reflect the crowd's implied probability of each outcome. Unlike traditional sports betting, trades are matched peer-to-peer; the platform does not take the other side of any bet.

A contract with exactly two possible outcomes, settling at $1.00 if the event occurs and $0.00 if it does not. The market price at any moment reflects the crowd's implied probability of the event happening.

A strategy that buys both the YES and NO sides of the same binary market simultaneously, when their combined purchase price falls below the guaranteed $1.00 settlement value. Because one side must always pay out a dollar, the profit is locked in at the moment of purchase regardless of the outcome.

An electronic matching system that ranks and matches buy and sell orders continuously by price and time priority. Polymarket uses a hybrid version: orders are collected through a centralized system for speed, but final settlement is recorded on the blockchain.

A dollar-pegged stablecoin where one USDC equals one U.S. dollar. It can be transferred on public blockchains instantly and without bank intermediaries, making it suitable for settling prediction-market trades.

A charge levied on traders who execute against existing orders in a limit-order book, thereby removing liquidity. Makers — who post resting orders that add liquidity — typically pay no fee or receive a rebate. Taker fees disproportionately affect high-frequency bots that continuously take liquidity rather than provide it.

A participant who posts continuous two-sided quotes — both buy and sell — in a market, profiting from the bid-ask spread. Market makers provide the liquidity that lets other participants trade immediately; on Polymarket they pay zero taker fees and receive rebates funded by taker-fee revenue.

repos.summary: An open-source bot that monitors Polymarket and Kalshi simultaneously for mispriced Bitcoin contracts, buying the cheaper side on one platform when the combined YES+NO cost falls below $1.00. Implements cross-platform rather than intramarket arbitrage, exploiting price divergence between two separate prediction-market liquidity pools. Emerged from the community of traders attempting to reverse-engineer and replicate gabagool22's results.

A bot targeting Polymarket's 15-minute Bitcoin binary markets that implements the intramarket spread-capture strategy gabagool22 popularized. Monitors the order book for YES+NO pairs priced below parity and executes both legs automatically. One of several GitHub implementations that surfaced after @thejayden's article circulated widely on X.

fact_check: The tweet claims gabagool22 made '$500k in a single month.' On-chain analytics show cumulative verified profits of approximately $788,000 over roughly three months of operation — implying a monthly average closer to $250,000–$260,000. No authenticated snapshot of a single calendar month showing $500,000+ in net profit has been identified in primary sources. The cumulative figure is substantial and verifiable; the per-month framing appears to be an approximation or an intermediate snapshot rather than a precisely documented monthly total.
